clue.text: Grim situation for a Tiller girl ?

parts.note: grim and stern both describe a forbidding, severe manner
a post is a job or position, a situation in the employment sense

explanation.surface: A dancer from the Tiller Girls troupe finds herself in a bleak predicament.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tiller Girls were a famous British high-kicking dance troupe; here 'Tiller girl' is re-read as the ship's timber (ships are 'she') that carries the rudder and its tiller.
explanation.definitionFit: The upright timber at a vessel's stern is where the rudder, worked by the tiller, is hung, so it partners the tiller.

clue.text: Sailor has a club in the cellar

parts.note: an old salt is a seasoned sailor
a spoon was an old name for a lofted wooden golf club

explanation.surface: A seaman keeps a cudgel down in the basement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cellar' looks like a basement, but it is the salt cellar at table, where this little utensil lives.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny utensil kept in a salt cellar for serving the condiment at table.

clue.text: Little creature takes me back and forth to the front

indicators.note: back tells us to write the word me in reverse order
the front of the word to means only its opening letter is used

explanation.surface: A tiny animal carries the speaker to and fro towards the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'me back and forth' gives ME backwards (EM) then ME forwards; 'the front' of 'to' adds T.
explanation.definitionFit: An emmet is a dialect word for an ant, a small insect.

clue.text: Bring back beat with range of notes

indicators.note: bring back asks for the word for beat to be turned round

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
the Urals are a mountain range in Russia

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a rhythm that spans a wide set of musical pitches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring back' reverses TAN to NAT; 'range' looks musical but is the Ural mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, naturals are notes that are neither sharp nor flat.

clue.text: Terrible about red who is hard-hearted

indicators.note: something terrible is in a bad state, so the letters are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A dreadful tale about a communist who shows no pity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' rearranges the letters of ABOUT and RED together.
explanation.definitionFit: Obdurate means stubbornly unmoved, unfeeling and unyielding to pleas.

clue.text: Sent back to start urban development in Devon

indicators.note: to start says that the word to stands at the beginning

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: sent back means the word sent is read in reverse

explanation.surface: Someone is sent back to begin a new housing project in the West Country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the word 'Sent' round and 'to start' puts 'to' at the front. Devon is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Totnes is a market town in Devon, so it is a settlement there.

clue.text: Path of a heavenly (and with-it) sphere.

indicators.note: with places the second piece alongside the first

parts.note: an orb is a globe or ball
taken as written

explanation.surface: A celestial globe, fashionable and up to date, follows its course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with-it' looks like slang for trendy, but it is 'with' joining IT to ORB.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavenly body follows a curved track round a star or planet: its course.

clue.text: A monastic type looks like an orange

definitions.meaning: a layperson dedicated to a religious order
a sphere flattened at the poles, the shape of an orange

explanation.surface: A monk resembles a citrus fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a lay person attached to a monastery, and the geometric term for a sphere squashed at its poles.

clue.text: Circe knew how to make champagne dry ?

definitions.text: Circe knew how to make champagne dry ?

parts.words: Circe knew how to make champagne dry ?
parts.note: read as a coined verb, making something 'brut', the term for very dry champagne; Circe turned men into beasts

explanation.surface: An enchantress was skilled at producing a dry sparkling wine.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth the witch Circe turned Odysseus's men into swine; BRUT is the label for the driest champagne, so 'make brut' is a second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To degrade into a beast, as Circe did to men, or punningly to render wine brut.

clue.text: Appointment to investigate a good man's crime

parts.note: to try a case is to investigate it judicially
St, short for saint, is the crossword good man

explanation.surface: A meeting is arranged to look into a virtuous man's offence.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as putting a saint on trial for his crime; 'crime' completes that picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a prearranged meeting, especially between lovers.

clue.text: Told story about German with restricted meaning

indicators.note: about means the first word goes round the second

parts.note: to lie is to tell a story, so told story is lied
mit is the German word for with

explanation.surface: A narrator spun a tale about a German, with a narrow sense of meaning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' looks like a link word, but it is translated into German and sits inside the word for 'told story'.
explanation.definitionFit: Limited means kept within bounds, confined.

clue.text: Docks shoddily built by the railway

indicators.note: shoddily built means put together badly, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: Ry is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Wharves badly constructed beside the train line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoddily' says the letters of 'built' are jumbled; 'Docks' looks like a verb but names the Thames port.
explanation.definitionFit: Tilbury is a port on the Thames in Essex, famous for its docks.

clue.text: Thank you, sir — must go out for an instrument

indicators.note: the word sir must go on the outside, wrapping the other piece

parts.note: taken as written
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: A grateful dismissal: thanks, sir, now leave in exchange for a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thank you' is British slang shortened to two letters; 'must go out' means 'sir' sits on the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitar is a long-necked Indian stringed instrument.

clue.text: Between salient points,-like home-bound astronauts

definitions.meaning: an inward-pointing angle lying between projecting ones
space travellers returning to Earth come back into the atmosphere

explanation.surface: Space travellers heading home pass between projecting points.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: in fortification, an angle pointing inward, and, read as re-entering, describing a returning spacecraft.

clue.text: Kiss of death for the big copper?

parts.note: OS is the abbreviation for outsize
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
late means dead, the deceased

explanation.surface: A fatal kiss for a large policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but is the chemical element, symbol CU.
explanation.definitionFit: To osculate is a formal or jocular verb meaning to kiss.

clue.text: Stick on device for going .'slowly in the 'thicket

parts.note: a cane is a walking stick
a brake is the device used to slow a vehicle

explanation.surface: A walking stick fitted with a braking device in the undergrowth.
explanation.definitionFit: A canebrake is a dense thicket of cane plants.

clue.text: Take care of one's intellect

definitions.meaning: the faculty of thinking and reason

explanation.surface: Look after your brain.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: as a verb, to look after; as a noun, the faculty of thought.

clue.text: Fog signal observed up on a hill

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: noted means observed
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A foghorn-like warning was seen on a hilltop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the word for 'observed', since this is a down clue. A railway detonator is a small charge laid on the track.
explanation.definitionFit: On railways a detonator is a small charge placed on the line that bangs as a warning in fog.

clue.text: Evinced by those not liking to alter its dates

indicators.note: to alter is to change, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Disapproving people show it when told to change the dates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to alter' rearranges ITS DATES.
explanation.definitionFit: Distaste is the feeling of aversion that people who dislike something display.

clue.text: Instruments taken by a doctor in his travels

indicators.note: taken by means the first pieces are held inside another

parts.note: tours are journeys or travels
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, stands for a doctor

explanation.surface: A medic carries tools along on his journeys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken by' puts the two letters for 'a doctor' inside the word for travels; 'Instruments' here means drums.
explanation.definitionFit: Tambours are drums, so musical instruments.

clue.text: Morris needs so many men.

parts.note: ... Men's Morris is an old board game, so the clue asks how many men it takes

explanation.surface: A Morris dancing team is short of members.
explanation.walkthrough: Morris suggests the folk dance, but it is the board game Nine Men's Morris.
explanation.definitionFit: The board game is named for the number of pieces each player has.

clue.text: Light thread

definitions.meaning: the glowing wire in an electric bulb

explanation.surface: A fine strand.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the glowing wire in a lamp bulb, and any slender fibre.

clue.text: Failed to get the girl, did 'e say?

definitions.text: Failed to get the girl, did 'e say?

parts.words: Failed to get the girl, did 'e say?
parts.note: said with a dropped h, missed her sounds like a form of address for a man

explanation.surface: A man wonders whether he heard that someone lost out on winning the girl.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H in ''e' signals a Cockney accent, in which 'missed 'er' runs together into the polite title for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: The spoken words for having failed to catch her blur into the courtesy title used before a man's name.

clue.text: Wine makes a girl kind of square

parts.note: Clare is a girl's name
a T-square is a drawing instrument

explanation.surface: A drink turns a young woman into an old-fashioned square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'square' looks like a conservative person but is the T-square used in drawing.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux wine.

clue.text: Disorderly riot with cable car type

indicators.note: disorderly means out of order, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An unruly mob runs amok among the cable cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disorderly' rearranges RIOT and CABLE together.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabriolet is a car with a folding roof, a convertible.

clue.text: Suits or their containers ?

definitions.meaning: suitcases, the luggage that suits are packed in

explanation.surface: Legal actions, or the bags they come in.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: lawsuits heard in court, and boxes or luggage that hold things such as clothes.

clue.text: Stick it at the wicket ?

parts.note: to stick it out at the crease in cricket is to go on batting; the same letters give a stick

explanation.surface: Advice to a cricketer to dig in and keep batting.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words it means to carry on batting in cricket; as one it is a conductor's or relay runner's stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A short rod or stick, and also, split in two, continuing at the crease.

clue.text: The one right owned by them

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: The only correct thing belongs to that group.
explanation.definitionFit: A possessive pronoun meaning belonging to those people.

clue.text: Racial gunman

parts.note: racial here means to do with a race, a running event, and the gunman fires to begin it

explanation.surface: A gunman with a racist motive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racial' looks like ethnicity but means of a race on the track; the official with the pistol begins it.
explanation.definitionFit: The official who fires the gun to begin a race.

clue.text: One learning to be a noted prince

definitions.text: One learning to be a noted prince

parts.words: One learning to be a noted prince
parts.note: a learner, and one half of the title of the operetta The ... Prince by Romberg

explanation.surface: An apprentice training to become a famous royal.
explanation.walkthrough: The Student Prince is a well-known operetta, so this word before 'prince' makes a noted one.
explanation.definitionFit: A learner at a college or university; also the hero of a famous operetta.

clue.text: .Utter profanity of a south-west feature.

parts.note: the ear is a facial feature

explanation.surface: Someone curses about a landmark in the West Country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feature' looks like a landmark but is a part of the face.
explanation.definitionFit: To swear is to curse, to use bad language.

clue.text: Adjusted rate more-certain to be' official

indicators.note: adjusted means altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: surer means more certain

explanation.surface: A changed rate makes it more certain who is in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adjusted' rearranges RATE with SURER, the word 'more-certain' gives.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasurer is the officer responsible for an organisation's funds.
